description: Designs, deploys, and optimizes production Generative AI applications, RAG architectures, prompt pipelines, model evaluation suites, and guardrails.
default_interviewer_tone: Direct, technical, AI systems-focused; probes for latency, retrieval quality, evaluation metrics, and production failure modes.

suggested_certifications.name: Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer

question_style_notes.entry: Verbal problem-solving prompts on embedding retrieval, chunking trade-offs, and basic prompt testing on projects. No assumption of massive production LLM spend.
question_style_notes.mid: Production RAG evaluation, reranking pipelines, structured tool calling, latency optimization, and hallucinations mitigation.
question_style_notes.senior: Multi-agent workflows, semantic cache topologies, token cost economics, model distillation/fine-tuning trade-offs, and automated red-teaming.
question_style_notes.lead: Enterprise AI governance, safety compliance, high-volume inference infrastructure, and foundation model selection strategy.

skills.name: LLM Application Design & RAG
skills.description: Architects Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, semantic routing, vector embeddings, reranking, and context window assembly.
skills.rubric_l1: Passes entire raw documents into LLM prompt; ignores chunking, embeddings, or context overflow limits.
skills.rubric_l2: Uses basic naive RAG with fixed chunk sizes and cosine similarity; unaware of lost-in-the-middle phenomena or chunk fragmentation.
skills.rubric_l3: Designs advanced RAG pipelines utilizing semantic chunking, cross-encoder reranking, hybrid keyword-vector search, and metadata filtering.
skills.rubric_l4: Solves complex retrieval failures with query rewriting, hypothetical document embeddings (HyDE), and contextual compression.
skills.rubric_l5: Architects multi-hop reasoning graphs, hierarchical summary indices, and dynamic agentic retrieval workflows under tight latency budgets.

L2: Explains the difference between parametric model memory and non-parametric retrieved context.
Implements basic document chunking strategies and generates vector embeddings using standard embedding models.
Performs vector similarity queries against vector stores to populate LLM prompt context.
L3: Constructs hybrid search combining BM25 keyword matching with dense vector similarity.
Integrates cross-encoder rerankers to reorder candidate chunks prior to prompt injection.
Applies metadata filtering to isolate retrieval scopes by tenant, date, or document category.
L4: Implements query decomposition and transformation (HyDE, step-back prompting) to address ambiguous user questions.
Mitigates the lost-in-the-middle phenomenon by optimizing chunk positioning and context compression.
Designs semantic caching layers to serve frequent questions without invoking downstream LLMs.
L5: Architects agentic multi-hop retrieval workflows capable of iteratively querying disparate knowledge bases.
Benchmarks and tunes embedding vector quantization (HNSW vs IVFPQ) for sub-10ms billion-scale vector search.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose an application needs to answer questions based on a collection of PDF user manuals; talk me through how you would chunk, embed, and retrieve the right sections.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you improved the retrieval precision and recall of a RAG pipeline that frequently returned irrelevant or incomplete document excerpts.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you architected an enterprise RAG system that maintained high response accuracy while strictly respecting multi-tenant document permissions.

skills.name: Prompt & Context Engineering and Evaluation
skills.description: Develops structured prompt strategies, function/tool calling schemas, and automated offline/online LLM evaluation frameworks (Ragas, LLM-as-a-judge).
skills.rubric_l1: Relies on manual vibing checks; hardcodes unformatted prompts without temperature or system prompt separation.
skills.rubric_l2: Uses few-shot examples and system prompts but lacks automated regression evaluation datasets or systematic metrics.
skills.rubric_l3: Implements structured JSON output schemas, rigorous few-shot exemplars, and automated evaluation metrics (faithfulness, answer relevance).
skills.rubric_l4: Designs robust LLM-as-a-judge evaluation pipelines with calibration against human ground-truth labels and bias mitigation.
skills.rubric_l5: Establishes continuous continuous-eval CI/CD regression gates, synthetic dataset generation, and dynamic context budgeting engines.

L2: Structures prompts separating system directives, user instructions, and few-shot examples.
Enforces structured JSON output generation using schema enforcement or Pydantic models.
Collects test prompts to manually evaluate model response quality across iterations.
L3: Implements automated offline evaluation suites scoring response faithfulness, answer relevance, and context precision.
Designs tool-calling schemas with strict parameter typing, validation, and error recovery.
Constructs golden evaluation datasets representing edge cases and adversarial candidate inputs.
L4: Calibrates LLM-as-a-judge evaluators against human ratings to measure judge correlation and eliminate position bias.
Designs prompt optimization workflows that systematically reduce input token counts while retaining task accuracy.
Implements canary evaluation suites that gate model prompt releases on automated quality thresholds.
L5: Architects synthetic data generation pipelines with self-critique loops to train and evaluate domain-specific judges.
Develops automated regression detection that catches subtle semantic drift across model upstream provider releases.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose an LLM needs to extract product details from customer support emails and return a strict JSON schema; talk me through how you ensure it adheres to the schema.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you built an automated evaluation pipeline to test whether a prompt modification actually improved answer quality without introducing regressions.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you calibrated an LLM-as-a-judge pipeline to ensure its scoring aligned reliably with human domain expert evaluations.

skills.name: ML Fundamentals & Model Selection
skills.description: Evaluates foundational model architectures, parameter sizes, fine-tuning versus prompting trade-offs, and quantizations.
skills.spoken_topic_label: machine learning fundamentals and model selection
skills.rubric_l1: Views models as black boxes; confuses supervised fine-tuning with RAG; unaware of context window limits.
skills.rubric_l2: Knows common model families (OpenAI, Gemini, open-source) but cannot articulate when fine-tuning is justified over RAG or prompting.
skills.rubric_l3: Evaluates model selection trade-offs (latency, context size, cost, accuracy) and designs LoRA/PEFT fine-tuning pipelines when appropriate.
skills.rubric_l4: Optimizes models via quantization (AWQ, GGUF), knowledge distillation, and preference alignment (DPO, RLHF) for specific tasks.
skills.rubric_l5: Architects custom embedding model fine-tuning, domain adaptation on private corpora, and hybrid routing between small and large models.

L2: Compares open-weight models with hosted proprietary API models across latency, privacy, and operating cost.
Explains the difference between knowledge retrieval (RAG) and behavioral adaptation (fine-tuning).
Identifies tokenization behavior and explains how special tokens impact prompt execution.
L3: Selects appropriate model sizes (e.g. 8B vs 70B parameters) based on task complexity, throughput needs, and cost targets.
Prepares training datasets and executes parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA / QLoRA) for specialized formatting.
Evaluates tokenizer characteristics across different languages, code, and numerical reasoning.
L4: Implements model routing layers that direct simple tasks to small fast models and complex queries to frontier reasoning models.
Applies model quantization techniques to decrease VRAM memory footprint while preserving task perplexity.
Fine-tunes domain-specific embedding models using contrastive triplet loss to boost domain retrieval.
L5: Designs model distillation pipelines where frontier models teach compact on-device models for high-throughput edge tasks.
Formulates alignment strategies utilizing Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to correct undesirable model behaviors.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose your team needs to decide between using a hosted frontier model API versus self-hosting an open-source model; talk me through the factors you would weigh.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you evaluated whether a specific customer workflow required fine-tuning a model or could be solved through in-context few-shot prompting.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you designed a dynamic model routing architecture that cut LLM operational expenditure without reducing output quality.

skills.name: Production AI Systems (latency, cost, monitoring, guardrails)
skills.description: Engineers production streaming inference, input/output guardrails (NeMo, Llama Guard), token cost management, rate limits, and observability.
skills.rubric_l1: Deploys blocking LLM calls in UI threads; no monitoring of token costs, rate limits, or safety guardrails.
skills.rubric_l2: Implements streaming responses and basic rate limiting but lacks guardrails for prompt injection or system monitoring.
skills.rubric_l3: Implements production streaming with TTFT optimization, token spend budgets, and content safety filters (PII, injection defense).
skills.rubric_l4: Architects comprehensive guardrail layers (speculative execution, semantic safety checks), fallback model cascades, and distributed tracing.
skills.rubric_l5: Designs enterprise-scale inference infrastructure handling thousands of concurrent tokens/sec with sub-second time-to-first-token.

L2: Implements streaming token generation (Server-Sent Events / WebSockets) to reduce perceived user latency.
Monitors basic API error codes (429 Rate Limit, 503 Overloaded) and implements exponential backoff.
Applies basic keyword regex or prompt boundary tags to resist obvious prompt injection attempts.
L3: Instruments time-to-first-token (TTFT) and tokens-per-second (TPS) metrics across production LLM endpoints.
Integrates input/output guardrails to filter Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and harmful content.
Configures automated failover cascades to secondary providers when primary LLM APIs experience outages.
L4: Designs multi-stage defense against indirect prompt injection and jailbreaking across untrusted external documents.
Optimizes end-to-end user latency using speculative decoding, prompt caching, or streaming parallel tool execution.
Builds granular cost attribution tracking token expenditure per tenant and user workflow.
L5: Architects high-throughput self-hosted inference clusters (vLLM / TensorRT-LLM) optimizing continuous batching and KV-cache utilization.
Establishes automated red-teaming frameworks continuously probing model endpoints for adversarial vulnerabilities.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose users report that your AI assistant feels slow to respond; talk me through how you would measure latency and improve perceived speed.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you defended an AI application that accepts untrusted user uploads against indirect prompt injection attacks.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you architected a high-concurrency LLM service to guarantee sub-second time-to-first-token while controlling operating costs.

skills.name: Data & Retrieval Pipelines
skills.description: Constructs data ingestion pipelines, document parsing (OCR, tables, layout analysis), vector index synchronization, and deduplication.
skills.rubric_l1: Copies unstructured text directly into database without cleaning, schema extraction, or chunk metadata.
skills.rubric_l2: Parses basic text files but fails on scanned PDFs, complex tables, duplicate documents, and vector index updates.
skills.rubric_l3: Builds robust ETL pipelines extracting text and tables from complex documents, maintaining vector store freshness and metadata sync.
skills.rubric_l4: Designs incremental change-data-capture (CDC) pipelines synchronizing enterprise databases with vector indexes with exactly-once semantics.
skills.rubric_l5: Architects multimodal ingestion systems handling diagrams, audio, and tables with semantic graph linkages and automated lineage.

L2: Extracts text and structure from standard document formats (Markdown, HTML, plain text).
Attaches essential metadata (source URI, timestamp, author) to ingested document chunks.
Handles basic file parsing exceptions and formats inputs cleanly before embedding generation.
L3: Constructs document ingestion pipelines that accurately preserve tabular structures and section hierarchies.
Implements document deduplication and near-duplicate hashing (MinHash / SimHash) to prevent index pollution.
Schedules vector index update jobs that purge stale embeddings when documents are modified or deleted.
L4: Builds change-data-capture (CDC) pipelines synchronizing transactional database mutations with vector stores in real time.
Integrates layout-aware vision models to extract complex multi-column documents and embedded charts.
Establishes automated data validation checks that prevent corrupted or empty chunks from entering production vector indices.
L5: Architects distributed streaming ingestion pipelines processing millions of daily documents with end-to-end data lineage.
Constructs hybrid knowledge graphs connecting unstructured text embeddings with structured relational entities.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose you need to ingest technical documentation that includes markdown tables and code snippets; talk me through how you would parse and preserve that structure.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you built a pipeline to keep a vector database synchronized with a live document repository where files are constantly added, updated, and deleted.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you handled ingestion and indexing for complex multimodal documents containing both text and dense architectural diagrams.

skills.name: Project & Experience Deep-Dive
skills.description: Structured walkthrough of the candidate's own projects and work: scope, ownership, architecture decisions, trade-offs, and outcomes. Follow-ups probe what the candidate actually said they built.
skills.rubric_l1: Cannot describe any project coherently; vague about own role, stack, or outcome; claims work without substance.
skills.rubric_l2: Describes a project at surface level; can name the stack and own tasks but struggles with design decisions, trade-offs, or measurable outcomes.
skills.rubric_l3: Clearly explains a real project: goal, architecture, own ownership, technologies used, and key trade-offs with reasons; can dive one level deeper on any part when probed.
skills.rubric_l4: Deep command of own work: quantified outcomes, alternatives considered, failure modes handled, and how constraints shaped the design; connects project decisions to broader engineering principles.
skills.rubric_l5: Exceptional narrative and reflection: articulates the business/technical context, led non-trivial trade-offs, mentors others through the reasoning, and honestly separates team work from individual contribution.

l2: Names the project goal, stack, and their own tasks.
l3: Explains the architecture and their specific ownership area.
Justifies key design or technology choices with trade-offs.
l4: Quantifies outcomes or impact (performance, scale, users, grades of improvement).
Handles a follow-up on any component they described without hand-waving.
l5: Reflects on what they would change with hindsight and why.

question_patterns.anchor: Walk me through the most significant project you have built or contributed to — what it does, your role, and the stack you chose.
question_patterns.anchor_alt: Pick any project, class assignment, or hackathon you enjoyed — what did you build and what did you personally work on?
question_patterns.escalation: If that project had to serve 10x the users or data tomorrow, what would break first and what would you change?
probes: Why did you choose that stack over the alternatives you considered?
What was the hardest bug or setback in that project, and how did you resolve it?
Which part are you proudest of, and which part would you rebuild differently now?
How did you verify it actually worked — tests, metrics, or user feedback?
